excerpt:
| Symbology | Function | Accepted input |
|-----------|----------|----------------|
| Code 128 | `code128()` | Printable ASCII; Code Sets A/B/C with automatic optimal switching |
| Code 39 | `code39()` | The 43-character set: digits, `A`–`Z`, space, and ``- . $ / + %`` |
| Code 39 (Extended) | `code39ext()` | Full ASCII (128 characters) via two-character shift encoding |
| EAN-13 | `ean13()` | 12 digits (check digit computed), or 13 with `allow_check_digit_input=True` |
| EAN-8 | `ean8()` | 7 digits (check digit computed), or 8 with `allow_check_digit_input=True` |
| UPC-A | `upca()` | 11 digits (check digit computed), or 12 with `allow_check_digit_input=True` |
| UPC-E | `upce()` | An 11- or 12-digit number-system-0 GTIN-12, zero-suppressed to UPC-E |
| QR Code | `qr()` | Text in numeric, alphanumeric, byte (Latin-1), or Kanji mode; Model 2, versions 1–40 |
classification_basis: A real, checkable per-symbology accepted-input reference table (character sets, digit counts, check-digit rules, QR encoding modes) that is genuinely missing from the candidate -- the candidate's API Reference lists function signatures and option types but never states what raw input each accepts.

verification.evidence_note: Cross-checked each row against real encoder/standards source: upce.py docstring confirms 'GTIN-12 is not zero-suppressible into a valid UPC-E form' (GTIN-12/zero-suppression claim, real); code39.py's expand_full_ascii + 43-char base pattern (from standards/code39) confirms the Code 39 character-set claims; code128.py confirms Code Set A/B/C automatic switching; qr's standards package (_MIN_VERSION=1, _MAX_VERSION=40 in encoders/qr.py) confirms versions 1-40, and standards/qr/bitstream.py's latin1_bytes()/kanji handling confirms the numeric/alphanumeric/byte(Latin-1)/Kanji mode list. Grepped candidate readme.md for 'GTIN', '43-character', 'zero-suppressed', 'Latin-1', 'Kanji' before this edit: zero matches -- genuinely missing, not redundant.
